source: Maha Upanishad, chapter 6 (VI.71–73 per A. Hattangadi's edition as cited on Wikipedia, 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam', read 2026-11-24): ayaṃ nijaḥ paro veti gaṇanā laghucetasām / udāracaritānāṃ tu vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam. Some editions read 'ayaṃ bandhur ayaṃ neti' for the first quarter. G20 India Presidency 2022–23 theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: One Earth, One Family, One Future'.

shots.art: Two neighbouring village courtyards at dusk divided by a low mud wall; on each side a small figure seen from behind, counting things into baskets; long shadows, a narrow feeling.

A softly glowing pearl-like sphere, painted all in clouds and sea with no land, no continents and no coastlines, floating in a rose and violet dusk sky, lavender clouds swirling around it like a shawl, a few stars.

A long shared table under a huge banyan tree at dusk, lanterns hanging from the branches, many people of all ages sitting together, small and seen from a distance and from behind, the low wall between courtyards now crumbled into flowering vines.
en: the whole earth is one family.
hi: ऐसी गिनती छोटे मन करते हैं।

shots.art: Many small wooden boats with glowing lanterns arriving from every direction across a calm sea at sunrise, meeting in a loose circle; no flags.
en: It comes from the Maha Upanishad.
